finding: All seven paired samples favor the adaptive route, but the median complete serialized-reference-floor benefit is only about 1.56%, insufficient for the preregistered 2% application-speed gate.
interpretation: The production-shaped adaptive hydraulics preserve physical and nonlinear-solver behavior. The large isolated Richards speed benefit is mostly not reaching the serialized FMR floor route, so backend/provider binding overhead must be attributed before further optimization.
next_action: Preregister and execute provider binding/cache-hit overhead attribution. In particular quantify repeated sampler construction, exact-key creation, cache scanning/table acquisition and analytical fallback rebinding on an already-warm cache.
nonclaims: This is not a performance failure; it is preregistered timing-equivocal.
No production admission follows from this result.
